questions.prompt: What did the Money Tree compare money to?
choices: A rock that stays the same
questions.explanation: The Money Tree taught that money is like a seed - plant it wisely and it grows into something wonderful!

questions.prompt: What promise did the four friends make?
choices: To spend all their money quickly
To fill their jars with wise choices
questions.explanation: Each friend promised to fill their magical jar with wise money choices, starting their journey to financial wisdom.
The 50-30-20 rule helps you balance your money: 50% for things you need, 30% for things you want, and 20% for saving!

questions.prompt: What did the Money Tree say strong roots represent?
choices: Your savings that help you weather storms
questions.explanation: Just like tree roots anchor and nourish the tree, your savings create a strong foundation for your financial future.

questions.prompt: What are the four branches in the Branch System?
questions.explanation: The Branch System organizes your money into four purposes: NEEDS (must-haves), WANTS (nice-to-haves), SAVE (future goals), and SHARE (helping others).

questions.prompt: When money is tight, which branch should you feed first?
questions.explanation: NEEDS always come first because they keep you safe, healthy, and able to learn and grow!

questions.prompt: Which are examples of 'earning leaves' mentioned in the chapter?
questions.explanation: All of these except finding money are ways to earn! The key is providing value through work, skills, or being part of a family.

questions.prompt: What makes someone an entrepreneur according to the Money Tree?
choices: Having lots of money to start with
questions.explanation: An entrepreneur finds creative ways to solve problems for others - and people gladly pay for solutions to their problems!

questions.prompt: What did the Money Tree compare flashy flowers to?
choices: Wants that are beautiful but don't last long
questions.explanation: Flashy flowers are like wants - they catch your eye and bring joy, but they don't produce the fruit (long-term value) that sustains you.

choices: Wait a full day before buying something you want but don't need
Exercise for 24 hours before spending money
questions.explanation: The 24-hour rule helps you avoid impulse buying. Often after waiting a day, you realize you didn't really need that want-item after all!

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between saving and investing?
choices: Saving is for rich people, investing is for poor people
Saving keeps money still like a rock, investing makes money work and grow
Saving is dangerous, investing is safe
questions.explanation: When you save, your money sits safely but doesn't grow much. When you invest, your money works for you, growing and multiplying over time!

choices: Putting all your money in one investment
Planting many different types of seeds in different places
Only investing in things your friends invest in
questions.explanation: Diversification means spreading your investments around. If one investment fails, the others can keep growing - just like a smart gardener plants different seeds!

questions.prompt: What are the Four Shields of Protection?
questions.explanation: The four shields protect your money tree: Emergency funds for surprises, insurance for big disasters, knowledge to spot scams, and diversification to spread risk.

questions.prompt: Why should young people care about protection?
choices: They have the most money to lose
Protection habits built young become armor when older
Young people face the most financial dangers
questions.explanation: Starting protection habits when you're young helps them become automatic. By the time you have more money to protect, you'll already know how to do it!

questions.prompt: According to the Money Tree, what happens when you share wisely?
choices: You lose money and become poor
More comes back to you in various forms
questions.explanation: The tree taught that sharing wisely creates a positive cycle - you receive connections, opportunities, and satisfaction that enriches your life in many ways!

questions.prompt: What are different ways to share according to the chapter?
choices: Giving money to those in need
Helping others grow their own money trees
questions.explanation: Sharing isn't just about money! You can share time, skills, support causes, and help others learn - all of these create more 'shade' for everyone.

questions.prompt: What did the Money Tree say was the most important truth?
choices: You need to be perfect with money
You don't need to be perfect, just intentional
Money is the most important thing in life
questions.explanation: The tree's wisdom: you don't need to be perfect with money. You just need to be intentional - making thoughtful choices that compound over time.

questions.prompt: What is true wealth according to the Money Tree's final lesson?
choices: Having more money than anyone else
Using money wisely to create the life you want and help others
questions.explanation: True wealth isn't about having money - it's about using money as a tool to build the life you want while helping others do the same!
